Definition: of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready:--swift.
BiblicalUsage: James says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. Jesus says agree with thine adversary quickly, while thou art in the way with him. And the father in the parable tells his servants to bring forth the best robe quickly for the son who has come home. Swift, in Scripture, is a virtue aimed at the right things: listening, peacemaking, and welcome.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that swiftness is not hurry for its own sake. I believe James shows the pattern: quick toward listening, slow toward anger, and the father shows the rest — quick toward the returning sinner, with the best robe already waiting.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of the Lord
